## Project Overview

Mocha is an open-source, general-purpose JavaScript testing framework designed to run tests in Node.js and browsers. [PROJECT_CHARTER.md:9-12][package.json]  
The repository is primarily a Node.js project with browser support, implemented in JavaScript with TypeScript type declarations and checked with TypeScript. [package.json][tsconfig.json]  
The visible toolchain includes Rollup for the browser bundle, Playwright for browser tests, ESLint and Prettier for code quality, NYC for coverage, Webpack compatibility tests, and Astro Starlight for the documentation site. [package.json][docs/README.md:1-6]  
The main runtime entry points appear to be `bin/mocha.js` for the command-line executable, `lib/mocha.cjs` for the core Mocha API, and `browser-entry.js` for browser execution. [bin/mocha.js:41-46][lib/mocha.cjs:168-188][browser-entry.js:90-100]  
The documentation website is a separate Astro Starlight package under `docs/`. [docs/README.md:1-6][AGENTS.md:142-150]

## Setup / Installation

Install Node.js `^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0`; Node.js 22 LTS is recommended locally. [AGENTS.md:22-27][.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:6-12]  
Use npm for this repository; yarn and pnpm are explicitly disallowed. [AGENTS.md:22-27][.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:6-12]  
Install Google Chrome if you intend to run browser tests locally. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:6-12]  
Clone or fork the repository, then run `npm install` from the repository root. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:13-19]  
For a clean CI-style installation, use `npm ci --ignore-scripts`; normal local bootstrap uses `npm install`. [AGENTS.md:47-53]  
Some optional dependencies may fail during `npm install`; those failures can generally be ignored unless you are building the documentation. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:13-19]  
For documentation work, install the documentation package separately with `cd docs && npm install`. [AGENTS.md:47-53]  
The evidence does not show any required project-specific environment variables for ordinary setup; `.env` and `.env.test` are ignored, while documentation describes `MOCHA_OPTIONS` as a runtime configuration variable rather than an installation requirement. [.gitignore][docs/src/content/docs/running/configuring.mdx:52-62]

## Running Locally

Run `npm test` to execute the repository’s full validation command, including linting and Node.js and browser testing. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:20-34]  
Run `npm run clean` followed by `npm run build` to regenerate the browser bundle manually. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:55-65][AGENTS.md:37-42]  
The build uses Rollup, and the generated artifacts are `mocha.js` and `mocha.js.map`; these files must not be edited directly. [package.json][AGENTS.md:37-42]  
Run `npm run test-smoke` for a quick boot check, `npm run tsc` for TypeScript checking, and `npm run lint` for linting and formatting checks. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:20-34]  
Run `npx mocha --watch test/unit/` for a focused watch-mode development cycle. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:20-54]  
Browser validation is available through `npm run test-browser`; that script cleans, builds, and then runs the browser test scripts. [package.json][AGENTS.md:87-92]  
The documentation site can be run with `cd docs`, `npm i`, `npm run generate`, and `npm run dev`. [docs/README.md:7-17]  
The evidence does not identify a fixed local development port for either the core project or the documentation site. [package.json][docs/package.json]

## Project Structure

`bin/` contains the command-line executable, including `bin/mocha.js`. [bin/mocha.js:41-46]  
`lib/` contains the core implementation, including the Mocha API, CLI handling, runners, suites, tests, hooks, reporters, browser utilities, Node.js utilities, plugins, and type declarations. [lib/mocha.cjs:168-188][lib/cli/cli.js:24-36][lib/runner.js:1195-1224][lib/suite.js:417-445][lib/types.d.ts:19-26]  
`lib/cli/` implements argument parsing, configuration lookup, file discovery, command execution, Node flags, and watch mode. [lib/cli/run.cjs:30-48][lib/cli/config.cjs:17-26][lib/cli/lookup-files.js:32-51][lib/cli/watch-run.cjs:444-500]  
`lib/reporters/` contains built-in reporters such as HTML, JSON, JSON stream, TAP, XUnit, Spec, and Nyan. [lib/reporters/html.js:58-88][lib/reporters/json.js:108-123][lib/reporters/json-stream.js:66-87][lib/reporters/tap.js:150-185][lib/reporters/xunit.js:119-148]  
`docs/` is a separate Astro Starlight documentation package with content under `docs/src/content/docs/`, its own `package.json`, and its own TypeScript configuration. [docs/README.md:1-6][docs/package.json][docs/tsconfig.json]  
`test/` is divided into smoke tests, unit tests, integration tests, interface tests, reporter tests, browser-specific tests, compiler fixtures, plugin fixtures, and other behavior fixtures. [test/smoke/smoke.spec.cjs:12-14][test/unit/context.spec.cjs:6-8][test/integration/config.spec.cjs:30-32][test/interfaces/bdd.spec.js:25-27][test/reporters/base.spec.cjs:50-52][test/browser-specific/esm.spec.js:7-9]  
`example/config/` contains example Node.js configuration files intended to demonstrate available options rather than serve as application boilerplates. [example/config/README.md:1-7]  
`repro/` is an optional, separate minimal Node.js project for reproducing end-user behavior against the repository checkout. [repro/README.md:1-9][repro/README.md:12-35]

## Testing

The repository uses Mocha to test Mocha, with test scripts covering smoke, unit, integration, interfaces, reporters, JavaScript API behavior, browser execution, linting, formatting, and type checking. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:20-54][package.json]  
Run the complete validation suite with `npm test`. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:20-34]  
Run `npm run test-smoke` for the smoke suite. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:20-34][test/smoke/smoke.spec.cjs:12-14]  
Run `npm run test-node:unit` for unit tests and `npm run test-node:integration` for integration tests; the integration command includes a clean and build step. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:20-34][package.json]  
Run interface-specific tests through the BDD, TDD, QUnit, and exports scripts, and run reporter tests through the reporter test script. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:20-34][package.json]  
Run `npm run test-browser` for Playwright-based browser tests; browser tests require the generated bundle, and the repository’s safer script performs the clean/build sequence automatically. [package.json][AGENTS.md:87-92]  
Test files are visibly located in `test/smoke/`, `test/unit/`, `test/integration/`, `test/interfaces/`, `test/reporters/`, and `test/browser-specific/`. [test/smoke/smoke.spec.cjs:12-14][test/unit/context.spec.cjs:6-8][test/integration/config.spec.cjs:30-32][test/interfaces/bdd.spec.js:25-27][test/reporters/base.spec.cjs:50-52][test/browser-specific/esm.spec.js:7-9]  
The test suite uses `.spec.js` and `.spec.cjs` files, with fixtures also covering `.js`, `.cjs`, `.mjs`, `.ts`, and `.coffee` inputs. [test/unit/context.spec.cjs:6-8][test/integration/config.spec.cjs:30-32][test/compiler-esm/test-tla.mjs:4-6][test/compiler-esm/test-tla.ts:2-9][test/compiler/test.coffee:2-2]  
Visible testing patterns include `describe`, `it`, interface-specific `test`, lifecycle hooks such as `beforeEach` and `afterEach`, Sinon cleanup, and Chai or Unexpected-style assertions. [test/integration/fixtures/__default__.fixture.js:5-9][test/interfaces/qunit.spec.js:3-5][test/node-unit/buffered-worker-pool.spec.cjs:48-65][test/unit/context.spec.cjs:6-13]  
A focused watch command is `npx mocha --watch test/unit/`. [.github/DEVELOPMENT.md:20-54]  
The evidence does not identify a single repository-wide test setup file; setup and cleanup are visible within individual suites and helpers such as `test/integration/helpers.cjs`. [test/integration/helpers.cjs:347-349][test/integration/helpers.cjs:851-855]
